content_metadata.description: The video, presented by Craig Sigal, explores the significance of mental toughness, primarily focusing on overcoming overthinking and fear by staying present. Through visual analogies and narrative explanations, Craig addresses how overthinking is a natural brain function, akin to how a race car is designed to drive. He emphasizes the struggle to stop overthinking and the importance of grounding oneself in the present for optimal performance.

storylines.description: The video explores the concept of being present as a tool to eliminate fear, particularly in sports. Through narratives and analogies, Craig Sigal guides viewers in understanding the natural inclination of the brain to overthink and how grounding in the present can enhance performance.

but it's still very difficult for me to slow or stop overthinking.
The good news is it's not even necessary for you to do that to perform well.
When you're under pressure and sports, the mind likes to think even faster, and it's
just activating an old survival mechanism, a mental program to consider all the things
that could go wrong so that maybe you can prevent them.
It's just part of the fear response.
Unfortunately, this is not usually useful in sports.

your thinking.

they don't practice it and the advice is pretty much useless.
So here's the why and the how so that you can perform in the present moment and come
through brilliantly under pressure.
So the reason why this is really such a powerful tool for performing under pressure is because
pressure feelings, they come from a perception of fear.
Now you know that's mostly fear of failure, making a mistake, choking, not coming through,

We'll get this.

That's right.
